```{r}
#need to copy and paste file location to load data
VEHICLES <- read.csv("C:/Users/ryanf/OneDrive/Desktop/STA 9750/vehicles.csv", header=TRUE)
dim(VEHICLES)
```

```{r}
install.packages("dplyr")
library(dplyr)
library(regclass)
library(ggplot2)
library(randomForest)
options(scipen = 999)
```

```{r}
#checking blank counts
blank_counts <- data.frame(blank_count = sort(colSums(VEHICLES == ""), decreasing = TRUE))
print(blank_counts, max = nrow(blank_counts))
```

```{r}
#dropping unneccessary columns
VEHICLES <- VEHICLES[, !names(VEHICLES) %in% c("county", "lat", "long", "id", "url", "region_url", "image_url", "description")]
```

```{r}
#removing cars with 0 in price because listers purposely put cars up for 0 to have their cars show up on top when people filter from lowest to highest price based on the criteria
VEHICLES <- VEHICLES[which(VEHICLES$price != 0), ]
```

```{r}
#counting how many rows have a duplicate VIN and price, meaning the car has been put up for sale multiple times
sum(duplicated(VEHICLES[, c("VIN", "price")]))
dim(VEHICLES)
```

```{r}
#removing duplicated rows with same VIN and price since people will list their cars more than once for the same price
#sorting each row by date, and keeping the latest row of each distinct VIN/Price combination
VEHICLES <- arrange(VEHICLES, desc(posting_date))
VEHICLES <- VEHICLES[!duplicated(VEHICLES[, c("VIN", "price")]), ]
dim(VEHICLES)
```

```{r}
#removing rows where there are no vehicle type and vehicle size
VEHICLES <- VEHICLES[!(VEHICLES$type == "" & VEHICLES$size == ""), ]
dim(VEHICLES)
```

```{r}
#removing rows where condition and cylinders are blank
VEHICLES <- VEHICLES[!(VEHICLES$condition == "" & VEHICLES$cylinders == ""), ]
dim(VEHICLES)
```

```{r}
#sorting by most recent listing date to oldest listing date
#keeping the most recent listings for each VIN to and eliminate duplicate listings to prevent misleading results
VEHICLES <- arrange(VEHICLES, desc(posting_date))
VEHICLES <- VEHICLES[!duplicated(VEHICLES[, c("VIN")]), ]
```

```{r}
#reevaluating number of blank values
blank_counts <- data.frame(blank_count = sort(colSums(VEHICLES == ""), decreasing = TRUE))
print(blank_counts, max = nrow(blank_counts))
dim(VEHICLES)
```

```{r}
#removed rows with prices that were above 1234567 as the prices for the cars that were being listed above that value were unrealistic for the car that was being listed
VEHICLES <- VEHICLES[VEHICLES$price < 1234567, ]
summary(VEHICLES$price)
```

```{r}
#reevaluating blank values
blank_counts <- data.frame(blank_count = sort(colSums(VEHICLES == ""), decreasing = TRUE))
print(blank_counts, max = nrow(blank_counts))
dim(VEHICLES)
```

```{r}
#removing rows where condition is blank
VEHICLES <- VEHICLES[VEHICLES$condition != "", ]
```

```{r}
#reevaluating blank values
blank_counts <- data.frame(blank_count = sort(colSums(VEHICLES == ""), decreasing = TRUE))
print(blank_counts, max = nrow(blank_counts))
dim(VEHICLES)
```

```{r}
#removing rows with no type 
VEHICLES <- VEHICLES[VEHICLES$type != "", ]
```

```{r}
#removing rows with no manufacturer
VEHICLES <- VEHICLES[VEHICLES$manufacturer != "", ]
```

```{r}
#reevaluating blank values
blank_counts <- data.frame(blank_count = sort(colSums(VEHICLES == ""), decreasing = TRUE))
print(blank_counts, max = nrow(blank_counts))
dim(VEHICLES)
```

```{r}
#changing any rows with tesla as manufacturer to have electric fuel type since some rows with tesla say "gas", "other", or "hybrid"
nrow(VEHICLES[VEHICLES$manufacturer == "tesla" & VEHICLES$fuel == "other", ])
VEHICLES$fuel[which(VEHICLES$manufacturer == "tesla" & VEHICLES$fuel %in% c("other", "gas", "hybrid"))] <- "electric"
```

```{r}
#creating subset for values that are needed for this analysis
VEHICLES_subset <- VEHICLES[, c("price", "manufacturer", "odometer", "type", "condition", "year")]
```

```{r}
#evaluating blank values for VEHICLES
blank_counts <- data.frame(blank_count = sort(colSums(VEHICLES_subset == ""), decreasing = TRUE))
print(blank_counts, max = nrow(blank_counts))
dim(VEHICLES)
```



```{r}
#removing rows where price is less than $100 as listings under $100 were unrealistic
VEHICLES_subset <- VEHICLES_subset[VEHICLES_subset$price >= 100, ]
```

```{r}
#creating new column to group each car made into decade to group them to find association with decade
VEHICLES_subset$decade <- cut(VEHICLES_subset$year,
                              breaks = c(1900, 1910, 1920, 1930, 1940, 1950, 
                                         1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020, 2030),
                              labels = c("1900s", "1910s", "1920s", "1930s", "1940s", 
                                         "1950s", "1960s", "1970s", "1980s", "1990s", 
                                         "2000s", "2010s", "2020s"),
                              right = FALSE)
```



```{r}
#removing rows that dont have more than 20 listings of the same decade
VEHICLES_subset <- VEHICLES_subset[which(
  ave(VEHICLES_subset$price, VEHICLES_subset$decade, FUN = length) >= 20
), ]
```

```{r}
# creating sample of the cleaned data to use for analysis, due to processing capabilities I was only able to do 5000 rows
set.seed(9750)
VEHICLES_sample <- VEHICLES_subset[sample(nrow(VEHICLES_subset), 5000), ]
```

```{r}
#needed to remove listings with aston martin and harley davidson as they were just one listing for each in the dataset, it was not running the association analysis between price and manufacturer
VEHICLES_sample <- VEHICLES_sample[!(VEHICLES_sample$manufacturer %in% c("aston-martin", "harley-davidson")), ]
```

```{r}
#removing values that have na in odometer as the na values were causingerrors inn association analysis between price and odometer
VEHICLES_sample <- VEHICLES_sample[!is.na(VEHICLES_sample$odometer), ]
```

```{r}
#boxplot for price and type
ggplot(VEHICLES_sample, aes(x = reorder(factor(type), -price, FUN = median), y = price)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Price by Type", x = "Type", y = "Price")
```

```{r}
#association analysis for price and type
#needed to use windows function since the graphs were too large in the margins
windows(width = 20, height = 12)  
par(mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1))
associate(price ~ type, data = VEHICLES_sample)
```


```{r}
#boxplot for relationship between price and decade
ggplot(VEHICLES_sample, aes(x = factor(decade), y = price)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Price by Decade", x = "Decade", y = "Price")
```

```{r}
#association between price and decade
associate(price ~ decade, data = VEHICLES_sample)
```


```{r}
#boxplot to determine relationship between price and condition
ggplot(VEHICLES_sample, aes(x = factor(condition, levels = c("new", "like new", "excellent", "good", "fair", "salvage")), y = price)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Price by Condition", x = "Condition", y = "Price")
```

```{r}
#association between price and condition
associate(price ~ condition, data = VEHICLES_sample)
```


```{r}
#boxplot to show relationship between price and manufacturer
ggplot(VEHICLES_sample, aes(x = reorder(factor(manufacturer), -price, FUN = median), y = price)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Price by Manufacturer", x = "Manufacturer", y = "Price")
```



```{r}
#association analysis to determine relationship between price and manufacturer
#needed to created png in order to run association analysis successfully
png("manufacturer_associate.png", width = 2400, height = 1200, res = 100)
par(mar = c(15, 4, 2, 2), las = 2)
associate(price ~ manufacturer, data = VEHICLES_sample)
```

```{r}
#intital linear regression analysis and plot to see relationship between price and odometer as a whole
model <-lm(price ~ odometer, data = VEHICLES_sample)
summary(model)

plot(price ~ odometer, data = VEHICLES_sample)
```


```{r}
#association analysis between price and odometer
associate(price ~ odometer, data=VEHICLES_sample)
```


```{r}
#creating random forest model to see importance of each variable and how impactful it is to determining the price
rf_data <- na.omit(VEHICLES_sample[, c("price", "odometer", "year", "manufacturer", "condition", "type")])

Random_Forest <- randomForest(price ~ odometer + year + manufacturer + condition + type, 
                         data = rf_data, 
                         ntree = 500,       
                         importance = TRUE) 
varImpPlot(Random_Forest)
print(Random_Forest)
```


```{r}
#linear regression model for sedans made after 2000 using year and odometer as x variables to predict price
sedans <- VEHICLES_sample[VEHICLES_sample$type == "sedan" & 
                          VEHICLES_sample$decade %in% c("2000s", "2010s", "2020s"), ]
model_sedan <- lm(price ~ year + odometer, data = sedans)
summary(model_sedan)
```

```{r}
#scatterplot to show relationship of sedans made after year 2000 with year and odometer to determine price
ggplot(VEHICLES_sample[VEHICLES_sample$type == "sedan" & 
                       VEHICLES_sample$decade %in% c("2000s", "2010s", "2020s"), ], 
       aes(x = year, y = price, color = odometer)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "orange") +
  labs(title = "Sedan Prices by Year and Odometer",
       x = "Year", y = "Price", color = "Odometer") +
  theme_minimal()
```
